questions.question: A vehicle with air brakes traveling at 55 mph needs approximately ____ feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and actual braking distance. At 55 mph with ideal conditions, an air brake vehicle needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: You should stop and take a break ____ to avoid driver fatigue.
questions.explanation: Take a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent fatigue on long drives.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system operates the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles
Are easier to drive than single commercial vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. Because of this, they need more driving skill.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps keep an engine running properly:
questions.explanation: Keep your cooling system full of water and antifreeze at all times. Despite its name, antifreeze is important in hot weather too.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Turn off your signal after completing your turn or lane change
Only signal when another vehicle is nearby

questions.correctAnswerText: Only signal when another vehicle is nearby
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes, no matter if other vehicles are nearby. Start signaling early and keep it on during the entire turn. Turn it off when your turn or lane change is complete.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, the landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Always raise landing gear completely before driving. When uncoupling, lower the landing gear until it makes firm contact with the ground. If the trailer is loaded, turn the crank a few extra times to remove some weight from the trailer.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights
Use one set of turn signals

questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers whenever you park on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When checking your tires, which of the following is NOT a problem to fix?

options.text: Front tire tread depth of at least 4/32 inch

questions.correctAnswerText: Front tire tread depth of at least 4/32 inch
questions.explanation: Check for these tire problems: air pressure too high or too low, mixing radial and bias-ply tires, front tire tread less than 4/32 inch, and other tire tread less than 2/32 inch.

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove oil and water that build up inside the tanks. They can be operated manually or automatically.

questions.question: When you stop on the side of a highway, how far behind your vehicle should you place warning devices?
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle when you stop on the side of a highway.

questions.question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?

options.text: Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the brake pedal.
Reverse slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
Reverse slowly and apply the brakes with the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
questions.explanation: Move the vehicle forward slowly and use the hand control to apply the brakes. Make sure the air pressure is normal and the parking brake is released. If the brakes work properly, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is thin and clear enough to see the road through it. This makes the road look wet rather than icy.

questions.question: When should you test your service brakes?
questions.explanation: Test your service brakes before every trip. This helps you find problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: What should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights when driving in fog, even during the day.

questions.question: What are multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions used for?

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly.

questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions provide extra gears. They are controlled by a selector knob on the gearshift lever.

questions.question: If your brakes pull to one side when you use them, what does this mean?

options.text: The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, you have a brake problem. Fix this before driving. Operating an unsafe vehicle is illegal under federal and state laws.

questions.question: Are fully-loaded rigs more or less likely to roll over than empty rigs?

options.text: Just as likely to roll over.

questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity due to the weight of cargo. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: What should the driver of a double or triple do in poor weather?

options.text: Lead the way for other drivers.
Drive on the shoulder of the road.
Drive carefully because the vehicle is prone to skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully because the vehicle is prone to skidding.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, drive carefully with a double or triple. These vehicles are prone to skids, loss of traction, and rollovers.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.
